scope: Proposition 6.1 (Cleanup estimates) of the manuscript “Deterministic nonbipartite Ramanujan graphs in every fixed degree” (preprints/Deterministic-nonbipartite-Ramanujan-graphs-in-every-fixed-degree-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 178 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 6d8ea4bb85aae750), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 41. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Assume the early-phase estimates at l1, and maintain the structural estimators during cleanup. With the simultaneous discounted-account choice rule, the cleanup interval can be completed so that, at every chosen state, the precision matrices remain positive definite, (4.9) holds, and TS = X x∈S ex(x)2 ≤ nη , |Eij| ≤ 2Bk. The second inequality holds for every surviving pair (i, j) of total level k = ν(i) + ν(j). At primary points the lower estimate for T persists in the form T ≥ n−θ (n−1 + α/l)−1 . In particular the consequences (4.10) and (4.11), and a polynomial-loss form of (5.1), hold at l0.
